p: Want to make it out in time? The secret is to search like a detective and share like a team. Spend the first few minutes giving every corner a thorough going-over, and pool everything you find in one place. Look for patterns between objects, numbers and symbols, and talk through what you think each clue means. If you've hit a dead end, move on to something else for a bit. Coming back with fresh eyes often does the trick.

Because Woking station has frequent fast trains to London Waterloo, it's easy for friends coming from the capital to join a group, and handy for anyone visiting from across Surrey and Hampshire. The venue is only a short walk from the station, so you can be off the train and into the briefing in no time.

Woking itself has some fun extras to wrap around a game. Fans of The War of the Worlds can head to Horsell Common, just north of the town centre, where H.G. Wells had the Martians land in his famous story. It's now a big area of heath and woodland that's great for a walk. The Shah Jahan Mosque, built in the late Victorian era, is one of the earliest purpose-built mosques in Britain and a striking piece of architecture. For an evening out, the New Victoria Theatre hosts touring musicals and comedy, while the town centre's shops and restaurants keep everyone fed. If you've got a car and fancy something greener, RHS Garden Wisley is a short drive away, with glorious gardens and a huge glasshouse to explore whatever the season.
